material_findings.title: Deletion/addition asserted from double parentheses without uncertainty
source_quotes: (d) ((Not charge tuition or other fees from state-funded eligible students for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program))Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program, except that no fee may be charged for the following:
inventory_quotes: Deletion shown by double parentheses in proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d).
The proposal deletes WAC 392-425-040's prohibition on charging tuition or other fees to state-funded eligible students for TK enrollment.
The proposal adds sliding-scale TK enrollment fee authorization to WAC 392-425-040
material_findings.basis: The plain text contains literal double parentheses and no statement of their meaning; underline markup for new text is absent. The deletion/addition reading follows a WSR convention not evidenced in the supplied text (reference UI-05, UI-06). Both units carry uncertainty 'none'.
material_findings.practical_implication: Readers relying on these units take a convention-based interpretation as a source fact. The content of the bracketed text and the authorization sentence are otherwise reported accurately.

material_findings.title: Eligibility criteria recast as mandatory duties
source_quotes: (1) Children meeting the following criteria are eligible to participate in a transition to kindergarten program offered by an eligible local education agency:
(a) A child who has been determined, by the local education agency, to benefit from additional preparation for kindergarten through a screening process and tool; and
(b) A child who is at least four years old by August 31st of the school year in which they enroll in a transition to kindergarten program.
inventory_quotes: The local education agency must have determined through a screening process and tool that the child benefits from additional preparation for kindergarten.
A child must be at least four years old by August 31st of the school year of TK enrollment.
material_findings.basis: Source frames (a) and (b) as criteria defining who is eligible; it imposes no 'must' on the LEA to determine or on the child. Units 86 and 87 use 'must' with modality 'mandatory' and uncertainty 'none'. Unit 85 labels eligibility status 'optional'.
material_findings.practical_implication: Force labels overstate directive character. Read as conditions of eligibility, the units are accurate; read as duties, they are not evidenced.

material_findings.title: Declarative-future allocation language labeled mandatory
source_quotes: State funding for the transition to kindergarten program will be allocated to eligible local education agencies based on RCW  28A.300.072 and the state omnibus budget requirements. Funding allocations will be prioritized as follows:
(1) Eligible local education agencies that received state funding allocations for transition to kindergarten in the previous year will have priority for the subsequent year.
inventory_quotes: State TK funding will be allocated to eligible local education agencies; the allocating actor is not specified in this provision.
Prior-year TK funding recipients will have priority for the subsequent year's state funding allocations.
material_findings.basis: Assertion text preserves 'will'; modality field asserts 'mandatory' with uncertainty 'none'. Source uses predictive/declarative 'will be', and the reference recorded it as declarative future with unresolved year frame (UI-10).
material_findings.practical_implication: Low. Assertions are faithful; only the modality tag presumes a binding reading.

material_findings.title: Actor inferred for passive accounting duty
source_quotes: (e) Tuition and fees collected for students in classrooms receiving state funding for the transition to kindergarten program must be accounted for separately, in accordance with the requirements outlined in the school district accounting manual.
(2) In determining student eligibility and admitting students to a transition to kindergarten program, local education agencies must:
inventory_quotes: Local education agencies must account separately for tuition and fees collected for students in state-funded TK classrooms
material_findings.basis: (e) is passive with no stated actor. The actor is plausibly supplied by the (2) lead-in, but the lead-in's scope is 'determining student eligibility and admitting students', which does not naturally cover accounting. Unit cites only the (e) span.
material_findings.practical_implication: Actor assignment is a reasonable inference, not a stated fact. Scope mismatch between lead-in and (e) also bears on UI-07/UI-08.

material_findings.title: Permissive authorization under a 'must:' lead-in left without uncertainty
source_quotes: (2) In determining student eligibility and admitting students to a transition to kindergarten program, local education agencies must:
Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program, except that no fee may be charged for the following:
inventory_quotes: Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for TK enrollment, subject to the separately stated no-fee exceptions.
material_findings.basis: Modality 'optional' is the most natural reading of 'are authorized', but the sentence is item (d) under a mandatory lead-in and replaces text scoped to 'state-funded eligible students'. Unit records uncertainty 'none'.
material_findings.practical_implication: Low to medium. The permissive reading is probably right, but the structural tension and scope shift are unflagged.

reference_limitations: The frozen reference treats the deletion reading of double parentheses as unresolved; a reader applying standard WSR drafting conventions would regard units 94 and 95 as correct. The finding F1 is about evidentiary basis, not likely truth.
The reference's own force labels (declarative future for 065; permissive for 040(2)(d)) are interpretations; F4 and F6 record disagreement in uncertainty handling, not established error.
Reference assigned no unit-level duty to LEAs for (e) because the source is passive; F5 could be resolved either way by a legal reader.
unresolved: Meaning of double parentheses and status of undecorated text in WAC 392-425-040 (UI-05, UI-06).
Whether 040(2)(d) is permissive, mandatory-framed, or both (UI-07) and its scope relative to 'state-funded eligible students' (UI-08).
Timezone and receipt/postmark basis for all clocks and deadlines (UI-02, UI-03).
Function of the unlabeled 'September 8, 2026' and of 'RDS-7285.3' (UI-04, ID-09).
caveats_and_conclusion.overall_conclusion: Every source function in the frozen reference maps to at least one inventory unit, and the large majority of the 110 assertions are entailed by the quoted source text with appropriate absence statements for timezone, access details, and deadline basis. Material concerns are concentrated in the proposed rule text: deletion/addition asserted from plain-text brackets without uncertainty (94, 95), eligibility criteria and declarative-future language tagged as mandatory duties (86, 87, 102, 103, 104, 110), an inferred actor for the passive accounting duty (99), and five applicability fields that are truncated or contain non-source characters (88, 95, 96, 98, 99). Notice-side units (1 through 84) are substantively sound, with only low-severity glosses and one conflation of historical filing with amendment target (81). This is an advisory assessment; no score is given and completeness of the inventory against the source is not certified.
